claims.head: Power against power
claims.call: The Predators’ L1 (Forsberg, O'Reilly and Stamkos) spends at least 62% of its 5-on-5 time against the Avalanche’s first line.
claims.body: At home, the Predators keep sending Forsberg’s line (Forsberg, O'Reilly and Stamkos) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Andrew Brunette has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Avalanche’s first line is Lehkonen, MacKinnon and Nečas.
claims.nums: At home: 62% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 39% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Andrew Brunette likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Avalanche’s first line.
claims.cite: Matchups · Nashville home games this season · 5 games, 58 minutes for this group at 5-on-5

chips.tip: Nashville’s L1 (Forsberg, O'Reilly and Stamkos) at home: 62% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ first lines. Matchups, Nashville home games this season, 5 games, 58 minutes for this group at 5-on-5.
With no line matching, this group would face first lines about 39% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

notes.text: Gavin Brindley was added to the roster on Oct 15 and has played beside Parker Kelly and Fedor Svechkov.
Taylor Makar was added to the roster on Oct 24 and has played beside Parker Kelly and Logan O'Connor.
Zachary L'Heureux is no longer killing penalties: 3% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, down from 36% with his old team last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 9 games cover only 33% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 9th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Mavrik Bourque returned in their last game after missing 4 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Jayden Struble joined from MTL on Oct 10 and has played beside Nicolas Hague.

NSH.head: A tough matchup for the Predators
NSH.body: Even though Nashville has home-ice advantage, Colorado has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Predators’ best way through is a penalty kill that holds up.

COL.head: The matchup suits the Avalanche
COL.body: Even though Nashville has home-ice advantage, Colorado has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Predators can make it interesting if their penalty kill holds up.
